  label: oxabl-cache-admin reference

`oxabl-cache-admin` is the operator's command line. It talks to one server's admin API with an operator token: it creates and changes tenants, mints tokens, exports usage and checks health. Tenants then manage their own caches and members.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

It's in the server's container image. To run it on another machine, build it from the repository with `cargo build --release --locked -p oxabl-cache-admin`.

## Connect to a server

| Option | Environment variable | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--server <URL>` | `OXABL_CACHE_ADMIN_SERVER` | The admin API, such as `http://127.0.0.1:9091`. |
| `--token-file <PATH>` | `OXABL_CACHE_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE` | A file holding the operator token. |
| `--ca-file <PATH>` | | A PEM file of extra CA certificates to trust, added to the system's. |
| `--json` | | Prints JSON instead of text. |

The options go before or after the command. The token is only ever read from a file: there's no flag for the token itself, so it never shows up in your shell history or in a process list. `--token-file /dev/stdin` reads it from standard input.

The examples on this page set both variables first:

```sh
export OXABL_CACHE_ADMIN_SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:9091
export OXABL_CACHE_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE=$PWD/operator-token
```

The admin API listens on `127.0.0.1:9091` by default. Keep it off the public network. A region or a second deployment has its own admin API, so you point `--server` at it; there's no region flag.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. |
| `1` | The server refused. The error code and message are printed, such as `conflict: exists`. |
| `2` | A usage or configuration error, such as a missing `--server` or a bad size. |
| `3` | The server can't be reached: connection, TLS or transport. |

```text
$ oxabl-cache-admin health
oxabl-cache-admin: no server: pass --server or set OXABL_CACHE_ADMIN_SERVER
$ oxabl-cache-admin health --server http://127.0.0.1:9091
oxabl-cache-admin: no token: pass --token-file
$ oxabl-cache-admin health --server http://127.0.0.1:9191 --token-file operator-token
oxabl-cache-admin: server unreachable: error sending request: client error (Connect): tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)
$ oxabl-cache-admin health --server http://127.0.0.1:9091 --token-file bad.tok
oxabl-cache-admin: unauthenticated: unauthenticated
```

A `not_found: not found` from `health` usually means `--server` points at the public API (`8443`) instead of the admin API.

## health

Reports whether the database and the store work, and whether this node runs garbage collection.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin health
```

```text
metadata   ok
store      ok
gc_leader  true
```

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin health --json
```

```json
{"gc_leader":true,"metadata":"ok","store":"ok"}
```

## tenant

A tenant is one customer of the cache: a team or a company, with its own quotas, caches and members. Every command that takes `<TENANT>` accepts its id (`t_…`) or its name.

### tenant create

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin tenant create <NAME> [--hard-quota <SIZE>] [--egress <SIZE>] [--rate <N>] [--burst <N>]
```

| Option | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `--hard-quota <SIZE>` | The most data the tenant's caches can hold, such as `20GiB`. |
| `--egress <SIZE>` | The most data the tenant can download a month, such as `500GiB`. |
| `--rate <N>` | Requests per second. The default is `50`. |
| `--burst <N>` | The request burst size. The default is `200`. |

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin tenant create acme --hard-quota 20GiB --egress 500GiB
```

```text
id            t_6y5t0tqs0bjqccs5cnn168hm14
name          acme
status        active
hard_bytes    21474836480
egress_bytes  536870912000
rate          50
burst         200
created_at    1793740837
```

A limit you don't set is unlimited and shows as `-`. Running the same command again is a no-op that prints the tenant. The same name with different limits is refused:

```text
oxabl-cache-admin: conflict: exists
```

Sizes take binary units only: `B`, `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB` or `TiB`.

```text
oxabl-cache-admin: invalid size '20GB': use an integer with B, KiB, MiB, GiB or TiB, or 'none'
```

### tenant list

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin tenant list
```

```text
id                            name  status  hard_bytes   egress_bytes  rate  burst
t_6y5t0tqs0bjqccs5cnn168hm14  acme  active  21474836480  536870912000  50    200
```

### tenant show

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin tenant show acme --json
```

```json
{"burst":200,"created_at":1793740837,"egress_bytes":536870912000,"hard_bytes":21474836480,"id":"t_6y5t0tqs0bjqccs5cnn168hm14","name":"acme","rate":50,"status":"active"}
```

### tenant quota

Changes a tenant's limits. The flags are the same as for `create`; a flag you leave out keeps its value, and `none` removes a limit.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin tenant quota acme --rate 100 --egress none
```

```text
id            t_6y5t0tqs0bjqccs5cnn168hm14
name          acme
status        active
hard_bytes    21474836480
egress_bytes  -
rate          100
burst         200
created_at    1793740837
```

### tenant suspend and tenant resume

`suspend` refuses every data request of the tenant until you `resume` it. Both print the tenant with its new `status`, `suspended` or `active`.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin tenant suspend acme
oxabl-cache-admin tenant resume acme
```

### tenant delete

Deletes a tenant and all of its caches.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin tenant delete sports
```

```text
deleted t_4t8442shw8ecjday1cqf6ht9ev
```

After that, the tenant is gone:

```text
oxabl-cache-admin: not_found: no tenant 'sports'
```

There's no operator command to delete one cache. That belongs to the tenant.

### tenant bootstrap-admin

Registers the tenant's first human administrator, by the issuer and subject of their sign-in with an OpenID Connect identity provider.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin tenant bootstrap-admin acme --issuer https://accounts.google.com --subject 104729000000000000001
```

```text
id  p_3fan0y5h97qjxn9tjymsjqvppm
```

The server fetches the issuer's discovery document to check it. An issuer it can't reach is refused:

```text
oxabl-cache-admin: bad_request: the issuer could not be verified
```

## token create

Mints a token for a tenant and prints its secret once. Hand it to the tenant through a secure channel.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin token create --tenant <TENANT> [--expires <DAYS>d] [--name <LABEL>] [--scopes tenant:admin]
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--tenant <TENANT>` | The tenant, by id or name. Required. |
| `--expires <DAYS>d` | Lifetime in whole days, such as `30d`. Without it, the server's default applies. |
| `--name <LABEL>` | A label stored with the token. The default is `operator`. |
| `--scopes tenant:admin` | The only scope an operator can mint, and the default. Other scopes come from the tenant's own API. |

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin token create --tenant acme --expires 30d > acme-admin-token
```

```text title="acme-admin-token"
id          yezjdv5n30d039n9
expires_at  1796332844
token       oxc_<the secret, shown once>
```

## operator-token

Operator tokens are what `oxabl-cache-admin` itself uses. `oxabl-cache-server init` mints the first one; mint more here.

### operator-token create

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin operator-token create [--expires <DAYS>d] [--name <LABEL>] > second-operator-token
```

```text title="second-operator-token"
id          yte2r9snjk11yymp
expires_at  1801516849
token       oxo_<the secret, shown once>
```

### operator-token list

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin operator-token list
```

```text
id                name       created_at  expires_at  revoked_at
gracmfxahe4csv7a  bootstrap  1793740828  1825276828  -
yte2r9snjk11yymp  backup     1793740849  1801516849  -
```

### operator-token revoke

Revokes a token at once, by the id that `create` and `list` print.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin operator-token revoke yte2r9snjk11yymp
```

```text
revoked yte2r9snjk11yymp
```

The last valid operator token can't be revoked, because `init` never mints another one. Create a second token first:

```text
oxabl-cache-admin: conflict: last_operator_token
```

## usage export

Exports one calendar month of usage, in UTC, for billing.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin usage export --month <YYYY-MM> [--format csv|json]
```

The CSV has the header `month,tenant,cache,metric,value`, then one row per tenant, cache and metric, sorted in that order. `tenant` and `cache` are ids. The metrics are `stored_byte_days`, `ingress_bytes`, `egress_bytes`, `requests`, `lookup_ids`, `hits`, `entries_committed` and `compaction_bytes`.

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin usage export --month 2026-11 --format json
```

```json
{"month":"2026-11","usage":[]}
```

Use `--format json` for JSON here. The global `--json` flag doesn't change this command's output; it still prints CSV.

```text
oxabl-cache-admin: invalid month '11-2026': use YYYY-MM
```

## cache scrub

Re-reads and re-checks every stored pack of one cache now, by cache id (`c_…`).

```sh
oxabl-cache-admin cache scrub <CACHE>
```

```text
oxabl-cache-admin: not_found: not found
```

Tenants create caches through their own API, so this is for a cache a tenant has reported a problem with.
